headline: High: Cline can write shared workspace files while Khoj reads indexed notes, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can write workspace files and use MCP; Khoj reads indexed documents and notes. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge where malicious content in Cline-produced files could be ingested by Khoj. The shared filesystem path is documented, but no direct clipboard bridge is shown, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled instructions into workspace files that Khoj indexes or reads
IF Khoj treats retrieved file content as trusted guidance
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a read-only, curated notes directory
Separate Cline workspace and Khoj index paths
Add a file allowlist before Khoj ingestion
Mark generated files with a non-indexed suffix
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can read/write the workspace; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. If they share a workspace or indexed folder, sensitive code or notes can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs. Both profiles show filesystem access, so the leakage path is plausible in default-style local setups.
conditions: IF Cline and Khoj point at the same directory tree
IF Khoj indexes files that Cline can modify or create
IF source code or personal notes are present in that shared tree
mitigations: Use separate directories for code and personal notes
Disable indexing of the Cline workspace in Khoj
Move secrets and notes out of shared folders
Review Khoj’s indexed sources before enabling chat
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, while Khoj is read-only on the filesystem and does not modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct concurrent mutation conflict is limited. The main shared surface is read access, which is not enough for a higher severity.
conditions: IF Khoj is extended with write access to the same repository
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to one git worktree
mitigations: Keep Khoj read-only
Run Cline and Khoj on separate worktrees
Avoid letting Khoj edit files through plugins
Use manual commit review for Cline changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code and browser-derived content, and Khoj can retrieve and surface that content from indexed files. If Khoj presents Cline output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into user decisions or downstream edits. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary in the profiles, so the interaction is materially risky.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieves Cline-generated files and presents them as factual summaries
IF the user acts on Khoj output without checking the underlying source
mitigations: Require source links in Khoj responses
Ask Khoj to quote and cite retrieved files
Keep Cline-generated artifacts in a separate folder
Manually verify any action items before execution
requires-engineering: add verification prompts between retrieval and answer generation

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. If personal or regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, the pair can mix data classes with different retention and residency expectations. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated notes or secrets are stored in the same indexed folder as Cline workspace files
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated notes out of the shared index
Separate secret-bearing code from personal documents
Document retention settings for both tools
Purge indexed content after sensitive sessions
requires-engineering: align deletion and export workflows
